<reason>CON made the debate's most original move — distinguishing employer-linked financing from the US patchwork and invoking Germany/Japan/Netherlands as universal, work-channelled, multi-payer systems — and used it to reframe the clash as "one payer or many." But PRO turned that same evidence into its strongest weapon: those systems avoid the harms precisely because the state pays contributions when work stops, no fund may refuse, and the Dutch model isn't employer-routed at all. Since the motion's comparator is expressly "systems that tie access to work status," CON ended up defending the letter of employer-based insurance while abandoning its substance, and never escaped that bind ([B4.2]'s "financing base, not access" reply was a partial concession dressed as a parry). CON also left PRO's fragmentation/administrative-waste and single-buyer bargaining arguments essentially untouched across four speeches, which is an ignored live pressure. CON's best surviving lines — exit via fund-switching and the "budget line vs earmarked contribution" fiscal-vulnerability argument — were both met: PRO showed switching funds only changes the letterhead when the same national cost-effectiveness verdict binds every fund, and converted the "firewall" into a "fuse" (wage-based revenue contracts exactly when need spikes, with the treasury already in the loop via CON's own backstop). CON did land a real hit by extracting PRO's concession that outcomes "track funding, not payer count," and PRO's refusal to name a single-payer outperformer was a partial dodge of CON's Q1; that keeps the margin competitive rather than dominant. CON's clipped Rebuttal 2 is a further small execution cost. Both closings crystallized rather than dumped new material, but PRO's decision rule — care follows the person, not the paycheck, on the broadest revenue base — was the cleaner reason to vote.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO's [A2.1]-[A2.3] and [A4.5]: showing that every patch CON proposed (state-paid contributions for the jobless, no-refusal mandates) works by severing access from work status, so CON's showcase systems vindicate the motion rather than refute it. CON's counter that the motion concerns financing channels, not access, never fully dissolved the bind, and the admin-waste critique was left unanswered.</best_rebuttal>
